blurb:

blurb:
She came in from animal control a little underweight and a little uncertain, but Monica has been making up for lost time ever since. She's about a year old, 35 pounds, and a hound mix who has one full-time job: loving whoever she's with as hard as she possibly can. She's currently off-site in Mostly Mutts' Prison Pups training program, so she's actually learning real skills right now while she waits.

Her personality is genuinely sweet. Friendly with people, gentle, and happy as long as her person is nearby. She does have separation anxiety, so she needs a home where someone is around most of the day. A work-from-home setup, a retiree, a stay-at-home parent — that kind of situation. She's met other dogs at the rescue and done well, and another calm, social dog in the house would actually help her feel more settled. She got a little jumpy around kids running and playing, so a household with teenagers or adults is probably the better fit.

She is heartworm positive and will be treated, so this one is local adoption only. Once treatment wraps up, she'll be able to get back to normal activity. Call Mostly Mutts at 770-272-6888 to find out when she's available to meet — she's off-site for training, so you'll need to ask about timing before you head over.

blurb:
Rae has been through a lot. She came to Mostly Mutts from a neglectful situation along with three other dogs, went through animal control first, and needed a while to get her health back on track. She's about 10 years old, nine pounds, and a Terrier-Chihuahua mix. She's had her spay, a dental, and a mammary mass removal. She's doing well now and she's ready.

She's not a high-energy dog. Her daily routine in her foster home is pretty straightforward: nap, explore a little, collect some petting, nap again. She's friendly and sweet, but she's not going to climb into your lap and demand attention. She just likes knowing you're there. She lives with other dogs in her foster home and basically ignores them, which is honestly ideal if you have a laid-back dog at home who isn't looking for a wrestling partner.

One thing worth knowing: she's pretty hard of hearing. She responds better to louder sounds or a tap on the leg than to spoken commands. Mostly Mutts offers free lifetime training classes with every adoption and can help you figure out what works for her. She'd do best with older kids who understand that she's small and needs a gentle approach. Head over to mostlymutts.org or call to get the process started.

blurb:
Someone found Neo wandering on railroad tracks and made the call to help him. After a stray hold, two weeks at animal control, and a bout of pneumonia, he eventually made his way to Mostly Mutts. He's eight years old, 15 pounds, and a Bichon-Poodle mix with a fluffy little face and a lot of personality left in him.

He needs ongoing medication and monitoring, so he's a dog that requires a committed owner who's ready for that. What he gives back is real though. He loves being around his people, gets silly when he's happy — rolling around on the floor, making noise — and then turns around and just sprawls out quietly in a sunny spot. He's not demanding about it. Sometimes he wants to be in your lap, sometimes he just wants to be in the same room. He gets along well with other dogs and has mostly figured out how to be calm around cats, though he did chase them at first so a meet-and-greet would be smart. Older kids are a better fit since smaller kids moving fast can spook him.

If you're open to a dog with some medical needs and want a small, happy, grateful guy who's already been through the hard part, Neo is worth a visit. Reach out to Mostly Mutts at 770-272-6888 or through mostlymutts.org to learn more and schedule a meet.

blurb:
Darby has been through more than most cats her age, and she's still one of the sweetest animals at Mostly Mutts. She came in years ago as a nursing mom, raised her kittens, got adopted, had that fall through, and is now back looking for the home that actually sticks. She's six years old, nine pounds, and done waiting.

Here's what you're actually getting: a cat who follows you from room to room just to see what you're doing. She'll investigate your open cabinets, supervise the dishwasher, and eventually park herself on your lap for a long stretch. She doesn't meow much either. She'll open her mouth like she's about to say something and then just... doesn't. It's a whole thing. She also has extra toes, which is worth mentioning because it's genuinely delightful.

She's not a big fan of being held, so if you're looking for a cat to carry around, she's probably not your girl. But if you want a calm, affectionate companion who stays close without being demanding, Darby is exactly that. She's good with other cats and litter trained. Gentle kids are fine; just give her the chance to warm up first.

Mostly Mutts is in Kennesaw. Submit an inquiry through their website to start the process and arrange a visit.

blurb:
Darby has been through more than most cats will ever see. She came into Mostly Mutts from animal control six years ago while nursing three-week-old kittens, got all of them adopted, then landed in a home of her own. That didn't work out, and now she's back. She's litter trained, keeps her space clean, and at nine pounds she's not taking up too much real estate on that couch.

blurb:
Someone found Neo wandering on railroad tracks and stopped to help him. Good thing they did. After his stray hold at animal control, it came out that he had pneumonia. blurb:
Toby's foster family has a nickname for him: "the little artist." At two months old and about 1.5 pounds, he spends a good chunk of his day rolling onto his back and waving his paws in the air like he's painting something only he can see. It's ridiculous. It's adorable. You'd probably film it every single time.

He's playful and sweet, but he's also got a little independent streak that sets him apart from his eight siblings. When the rest of the litter is still going full throttle, Toby quietly excuses himself and puts himself to bed. He knows when he's done. That's a personality, not just a cat behavior, and it makes him genuinely fun to watch.

He's litter trained and microchipped. He hasn't been neutered yet because he's still too small, but Mostly Mutts covers that cost through one of their approved North Metro Atlanta vets once he's big enough, so this is a local adoption only. He's had his first round of kitten shots and you'd finish the series as he grows. If you've got a gentle kid at home or a cat who might enjoy a small, self-possessed little roommate, Toby's worth a visit. Submit an inquiry through the Mostly Mutts website to get started.
